history: Round 1 (this run). Found the piece already built across five prior rounds, fully documented in docs/ux-gauntlet/contracts/P3.md, committed through 8f0c78c9 with nothing uncommitted in the owned trees. Did not rebuild anything. Verified rather than assumed: ran tests/test_p3_*.py fresh, 107 passed, 2 skipped, both skips honest (a shared-settings-driven day-total drift and a gold mark whose break the plan no longer carries, both named in the test bodies, neither this piece's to fix). Started a private server on 8061 (KAIROS_AUTH_DISABLED=1) and drove the real endpoints: GET /api/plan/days lists the 30 days for the operator's own channel; GET /api/plan/day?date=2024-11-01 returns 76 breaks and totals matching the contract's documented shape (basis, unbound_placements, compliance); GET /openapi.json shows exactly the 7 path items and 9 operations the contract claims, 0 redefinitions. Confirmed every owned backend and frontend file is at or under the 450-line cap (largest: kairos_api/break_api.py 435, kairos/export/spots.py 449, OverrideDecisions.jsx 450, ScheduleEditor.jsx 442, DayBoard.jsx 449), matching the test's own > 450 threshold. Grepped every owned file for em-dashes and emoji: 0 hits. Grepped for TODO/FIXME/XXX in the owned backend modules: 0 hits. Confirmed the round-5 evidence screenshots referenced in the contract exist on disk (p3-r5-01-editor-money-and-check.png, p3-r5-02-editor-settlement-and-undo.png, plus three round-4 shots). Tried to view the live app in a browser to add a fresh screenshot: the claude-in-chrome extension was not connected, and Playwright's shared browser reached :3000 only as far as the login wall (no KAIROS_AUTH_DISABLED there), so no new UI screenshot was taken this round; nothing in this piece needed one, since the API-level and file-level checks above independently confirm the same contract the browser evidence already backs. All eight 'Raised, not fixed' items in section 9 of the contract are genuinely out of this piece's ownership (frozen kairos_api/server.py routes owned by other pieces, the frozen predicate contract, the settings write path, the shell nav split) and none regressed. Verdict: P3 passes all four bars as documented; closed nothing new because there was nothing genuinely open inside this piece's ownership to close. Killed the private port 8061 server at the end of the round.
